title: Jahorina & Bjelašnica: Sarajevo's Olympic Mountains in Winter
subRegion: Jahorina, Bjelašnica & Igman, the 1984 Olympic mountains above Sarajevo

bestPeriod.window: Late January-early March, with the first three weeks of February the most reliable window for depth on both mountains
bestPeriod.avoid: Late December-7 January, when Serbian and regional Orthodox holidays fill every Jahorina bed and the Poljice access road gridlocks; and after 20 March, when 1,300 m bases turn to mud
bestPeriod.raw: Late January-early March, with the first three weeks of February the most reliable window for depth on both mountains

accommodation.note: Jahorina 3-4 half board 90-160 BAM (€46, €82) pppn; Sarajevo city hotels €45, €90 per room

food.note: Mountain restaurant mains 14-25 BAM (€7, €13); Sarajevo ćevapi 8-12 BAM; coffee 2-3 BAM

transport.note: Airport transfer 60-90 BAM each way; hire car €30, €45/day; ski bus 10 BAM

activities.note: 6-day Jahorina pass 316-373 BAM, plus Bjelašnica days, Lukomir guided snowshoe, Trebević cable car

profile.difficultyNote: 3/5, five lift-served days on modest vertical, plus one full-day snowshoe traverse to Lukomir at 1,450-1,600 m that demands six hours on your feet

gatewayAirport: SJJ Sarajevo International, 30 km / 45-60 min to Jahorina, 27 km / 40-50 min to Bjelašnica's Babin Do
summary: Sarajevo is the only European capital with two Olympic ski mountains inside forty minutes of its trams, and the week works because you can move between them. Jahorina, which held the 1984 women's alpine events, is the bigger and better-lifted of the pair, a broad forested dome of long blue and red motorway with a good gondola and the largest floodlit night-ski operation in the region. Bjelašnica, which held the men's, is the harder, colder, wind-scoured mountain, its summit plateau rolling out into the shepherd villages of Umoljani and Lukomir above the Rakitnica canyon. The arc is Jahorina first for volume, Bjelašnica second for character, Sarajevo as the constant bolt-hole, and one non-ski day given over to the city's Olympic ruins. It suits confident intermediates who care more about atmosphere and value than vertical, and anyone who wants a European ski week for half the Alpine price.

itinerary.title: Land at Sarajevo, Baščaršija, and up to the mountain
itinerary.morning: Fly into SJJ, which sits in the Butmir plain ten minutes from the city. Collect a hire car if you have booked one, it is worth it here, because the two mountains are on opposite sides of Sarajevo and the bus schedule is thin. Change a little money: Bosnia uses the **konvertibilna marka (BAM/KM)**, pegged at 1.95583 to the euro.
itinerary.afternoon: Do not go straight to the snow. Spend three hours in **Baščaršija**, the Ottoman quarter, the **Sebilj** fountain, the **Gazi Husrev-beg mosque**, the coppersmiths of Kazandžiluk, and eat ćevapi standing up at **Ćevabdžinica Željo**. Then drive the 30 km up to Jahorina, a climb of some 900 m on a road that is properly winter-maintained but needs winter tyres.
itinerary.evening: Check in, collect hire gear from one of the shops on the Jahorina hotel road, and eat at **Koliba** at Hotel Termag, the best-executed traditional cooking on the mountain, in a stone-and-timber room.
itinerary.dayStats: SJJ to Jahorina 30 km / 45-60 min / climb from 500 m to 1,300 m / hire gear 120-200 BAM for six days / keycard deposit 10 BAM

itinerary.title: Poljice gondola, Skočine, and the width of Jahorina
itinerary.morning: Buy the **6-day Jahorina pass** at the Poljice window and ride the **Poljice 10-person gondola** up onto the ridge before 09:30. Warm up on the wide blues off Ogorjelica, Jahorina's pistes are unusually broad, which makes it a forgiving place to find your rhythm after a travel day.
itinerary.afternoon: Move west onto the **Skočine six-seater** and lap the long north-facing reds beneath it. These are the resort's best-preserved snow and its longest continuous descents; three or four laps here is a real day's skiing.
itinerary.evening: **Ski Bar Cassiopeia** at the Termag for the après hour, then dinner at **Restoran Vučko** in the hotel of the same name.
itinerary.dayStats: Jahorina 1,300-1,916 m / roughly 52 km of piste, 18 lifts / 6-day pass 316-373 BAM adult, 230-287 BAM child / lifts 09:00-16:00

itinerary.title: The Olympic run, Rajska Dolina, and skiing under lights
itinerary.morning: Ski the **Olimpijska staza**, the 1984 women's Olympic course, early, on the overnight groom, when the pitch is honest and the traffic is not. Then drop into **Rajska Dolina**, the sheltered eastern gully, and lap it; on a windy day this is where the whole mountain ends up, so take it first.
itinerary.afternoon: Lunch at **Rajska Vrata**, the timber hut restaurant at the foot of the Rajska Dolina lift and the most-photographed building on the mountain, order the beans with smoked meat and the somun bread. Ski until 16:00, then rest deliberately, because the evening is the point.
itinerary.evening: **Night skiing.** Jahorina runs the largest floodlit operation in the region, a session ticket is 58-69 BAM, a two-night pass 99-117 BAM, and the surface at −8°C under lights is usually the best of the whole day. Eat late at **Restoran Poljice** or back at the hotel.
itinerary.dayStats: Olympic run vertical roughly 400 m / night ski session 58-69 BAM (€30, €35) / floodlit hours typically 19:00-22:00 / two-night pass 99-117 BAM

itinerary.title: Cross to Bjelašnica: Babin Do and the men's downhill
itinerary.morning: Drive down through Sarajevo and up the other side, around 60 km and 75-90 minutes door to door, or take the ski bus for a 10 BAM supplement. Buy a **Bjelašnica day ticket, 59 BAM adult / 47 BAM teen / 42 BAM child**, at **Babin Do**, and ride to the 2,067 m summit ridge.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the **1984 men's downhill and slalom lines**. Bjelašnica is a colder, more exposed, more serious mountain than Jahorina, with less width and more consequence; if the wind is up, the top lifts will be on hold and you will spend the day in the lower half. Look across the plateau toward **Trnovo** and **Šator**, the newer lift development on this side.
itinerary.evening: Eat on the mountain at **Restoran Benetton** at Babin Do before driving back, or drop into Sarajevo and go to **Dveri** on Prote Bakovića for Bosnian home cooking in a room the size of a wine cellar.
itinerary.dayStats: Bjelašnica 1,266-2,067 m / day ticket 59 BAM (€30) adult / Jahorina-Bjelašnica by road 60 km, 75-90 min / no ski link between the two mountains

itinerary.title: Weather-contingency and rest day: Trebević, the bobsleigh track and the city
itinerary.morning: This is the designed flex day, take it early if a Dinaric low is dumping wet snow and closing the Jahorina road, otherwise take it here. Drive or bus into Sarajevo, leave the car, and ride the **Trebević cable car** from Bistrik: nine minutes and roughly 600 m of ascent to 1,164 m.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk fifteen minutes from the top station to the **abandoned 1984 bobsleigh and luge track**, a graffiti-covered concrete run through the pines that was used as an artillery position during the siege. Then descend and do the **Tunel spasa (Tunnel of Hope) Museum** at Butmir, which explains how the city survived. Finish with a steam at the restored **Isa-Begov Hamam**.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Inat Kuća** ("the House of Spite") across the river from the City Hall, then rakija at **Barhana** in the old town.
itinerary.dayStats: Trebević cable car roughly 9 min, base 583 m to 1,164 m / bobsleigh track free and unfenced / zero vertical metres skied / Tunnel Museum entry ~10 BAM

itinerary.title: Snowshoe to Lukomir, the highest village in Bosnia
itinerary.morning: Meet a guide, **Green Visions** is the established operator for this, and drive round to the Bjelašnica plateau, parking at or above **Umoljani**. Fit snowshoes and set off across the plateau. This is open, wind-blasted, treeless karst at 1,400-1,600 m and it does not forgive poor navigation.
itinerary.afternoon: Reach **Lukomir**, at roughly 1,495 m the highest permanently inhabited village in Bosnia and Herzegovina, a cluster of stone houses with stećci tombstones on the rim of the **Rakitnica canyon**, 800 m deep. In deep winter the village is largely empty and reached only on foot; the point is the walk and the emptiness, not a café.
itinerary.evening: Back down to Sarajevo. Eat at **4 Sobe Gospođe Safije** for something more ambitious, or **Kod Bibana** on the hillside above Vratnik for the view over the whole basin at dusk.
itinerary.dayStats: 12-16 km round trip on snowshoes / 5-7 hours moving / plateau 1,400-1,600 m / guided day roughly 120-200 BAM per person in a group / no EAWS avalanche bulletin, guide strongly advised

itinerary.title: A last morning on Jahorina, then out
itinerary.morning: Ski the Skočine side until midday on the last day of your six-day pass, the mountain is emptiest on a Sunday morning before the Sarajevo day-trippers arrive around 10:30. Return hire gear and reclaim the 10 BAM keycard deposit.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop into Sarajevo, eat a final burek standing up at **Buregdžinica Sač** on Bravadžiluk, and spend the last hour in the Baščaršija buying coffee and a džezva. Allow 60 minutes to SJJ with luggage.
itinerary.evening: Fly out. If your flight is early, sleep in the city rather than on the mountain, the Jahorina road at 05:00 in fresh snow is not a race you want to run.
itinerary.dayStats: Half-day skiing, roughly 1,500-2,000 m descent / keycard refund 10 BAM / Jahorina to SJJ 45-60 min / airport check-in 2 h for regional flights
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Colors Inn, Sarajevo (if overnighting before an early flight)

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Termag
accommodationStrategy.description: Stone, timber and sheepskin, a proper ski room, a spa, and **Koliba**, the mountain's benchmark kitchen. On the hotel road with quick shuttle access to Poljice and Rajska Dolina; half board matters because Jahorina has no real village and no supermarket. Roughly 130-200 BAM (€66, €102) pppn half board.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Bistrica
accommodationStrategy.description: The 1984 Games hotel, refurbished, still the biggest bed-block on the mountain and sitting at the Rajska Dolina base. Choose it for ski-in/ski-out and Olympic-legacy atmosphere rather than finesse, the practical family and group option. Roughly 90-150 BAM (€46, €77) pppn.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Colors Inn
accommodationStrategy.description: The counter-strategy: sleep in the city, ten minutes from Baščaršija, and drive to whichever mountain has the better snow. Halves the bed cost, doubles the food quality, makes the Trebević and Tunnel days trivial, at 45-90 minutes each way and no ski-in/ski-out. Roughly €55, €90 per room.

logistics.connectivity: Good on the pistes, patchy on the Bjelašnica plateau. Bosnia sits **outside EU roaming**, so EU and UK bundles do not apply, though the **Western Balkans "Roam like at home" agreement** and the 2023 EU-WB6 roaming reduction have cut charges sharply. Check your operator's zone before you land or buy a BH Telecom or m:tel prepaid SIM. Download offline maps: the plateau has dead ground.
logistics.emergency: **112** works; **124** is the ambulance. Mountain rescue is the volunteer **Gorska služba spašavanja (GSS)**, organised separately in the Federation and Republika Srpska, and helicopter recovery is not routine, assume a long ground evacuation. Bosnia is **not in the EU**, so EHIC/GHIC does not apply: carry insurance naming winter sports, off-piste and repatriation, and check that night skiing is not excluded.
logistics.weather: The Dinarics turn Adriatic lows into very heavy, wet snowfalls, 40-60 cm overnight is unremarkable, and the **jugo** that brings it can lift the freezing level above 1,500 m and ruin Jahorina's lower half in twelve hours. Behind it comes the **bura**, which puts Bjelašnica's summit lifts on wind hold. Sarajevo sits in a basin that traps a **severe winter inversion**, the city at −5°C under smog while Jahorina is at +2°C in sun.
logistics.bookingWindows: Jahorina beds for Orthodox Christmas and New Year (roughly 1-10 January) go three to four months out at double price; February half-term is the second crunch. Lift tickets need no advance purchase. The **Lukomir snowshoe day must be booked a week ahead**, it runs on demand. Trebević takes no reservations but queues on sunny weekends.
logistics.money: The **konvertibilna marka (BAM/KM)**, pegged at **1 EUR = 1.95583 BAM**. Cards work in hotels and larger restaurants; huts, the ski bus, taxis and Lukomir are cash. Jahorina ATMs run dry at weekends, draw in Sarajevo. Tip by rounding up to 10%.
logistics.transportRules: **Winter tyres are legally required from 1 November to 15 April**, with chains carried on mountain routes; verify the hire car is equipped. There is no vignette, A1 tolls are per section. Crossing into Croatia, Montenegro or Serbia needs the **green card** and written cross-border permission. Lift access is RFID keycard: 10 BAM deposit at Jahorina, 5 BAM token at Bjelašnica.
logistics.permits: No park entry fee. Bjelašnica parking is 2 BAM per started hour, 10 BAM daily. Drones need civil-aviation permission and are banned over the ski areas. **Landmine contamination remains a real hazard in parts of the Bjelašnica and Igman uplands**, BHMAC maps the residual risk; stay on marked pistes, marked routes and roads.
logistics.health: Sarajevo tap water is potable and good. There is **no daily five-point EAWS avalanche bulletin for Bosnia and Herzegovina**, FHMZBiH and RHMZ RS publish snow and weather data only, so treat all off-piste as unbulletined and carry transceiver, shovel and probe. Altitude is a non-issue at 2,067 m.

proTips: Buy the flexible **10-day combined Ski Card** rather than a six-day Jahorina pass if you intend to ski both mountains. It is valid non-consecutively across Jahorina, Bjelašnica, Ravna planina and Vlašić, which means you can chase snow between mountains instead of committing to one on day one.

Ski Jahorina on a weekday and Bjelašnica at the weekend, not the other way round. Jahorina takes the Sarajevo and Belgrade weekend crowd; Bjelašnica's weekend traffic is smaller and its lift queues barely exist.

Take the night-ski session seriously. At 19:00 in February the piste has refrozen into a fast, grippy surface that is better than anything you skied at midday, and the ticket is a third of a day pass.
Sleep in Sarajevo for the first two nights and on the mountain for the last four. You get the city's food and museums when your legs are fresh, and ski-in access when they are not.
Draw cash in Sarajevo before you drive up. Jahorina's ATMs are few and are routinely empty from Friday evening; the mountain huts, the ski bus and Lukomir are cash-only.
Walk to the bobsleigh track from the top of the Trebević cable car rather than driving the Trebević road. The road is often unploughed above the tree line and the walk is fifteen easy minutes.

Book English-language ski instruction in writing, ahead of time. Lessons here are extraordinarily cheap, 40-70 BAM an hour private, but the default working language is Bosnian/Serbian and turning up at the desk on the day rarely produces an English-speaking instructor in February.
Never leave marked ground on the Bjelašnica and Igman plateau without a local guide. This is landmine country as well as unbulletined avalanche terrain, and the two hazards compound.
Eat the mountain lunch at **Rajska Vrata** at 11:30 or 14:00, never at 12:30. It has perhaps sixty covers and everyone on Jahorina wants one of them.

raw.Pass tiers by name: Three products, not one system. **Jahorina (Olympic Centre Jahorina)** sells a resort ticket: **73-86 BAM adult/day (€37, €44)**, **53-73 BAM child (€27, €37)**, sliding across Pre/Post, Mid and Peak bands (peak roughly 22 Dec-15 Jan and 9-27 Feb). **6-day adult 316-373 BAM (€162, €191)**, **6-day child 230-287 BAM (€118, €147)**. **Bjelašnica-Igman (OC Bjelašnica)** is separate: **59 BAM adult (€30)**, **47 BAM teen 13-18 (€24)**, **42 BAM child under 12 (€21)**; Igman alone **30 BAM (€15)**. The regional super-pass is the **combined Ski Card**, a flexible **10-day ticket, most recently 350 BAM (~€179)**, usable non-consecutively across **Jahorina, Bjelašnica, Ravna planina and Vlašić**, over 100 km on one card. **Night skiing** is separate: Jahorina **58-69 BAM** a session, **99-117 BAM** for two nights; Bjelašnica **42 BAM**. **Keycard deposit 10 BAM at Jahorina, a 5 BAM token at Bjelašnica.** Buy at the Poljice and Rajska Dolina windows, at Babin Do, or online, no dynamic pricing and no early-bird on multi-day tickets, only autumn season-pass presale.
raw.Lift network and interconnects: Jahorina's spine runs from **Poljice** at roughly 1,300 m, where the **Poljice 10-person gondola** does the heavy lifting, up to the Ogorjelica ridge. The **Skočine six-seater** serves the long, wide, north-facing runs on the western flank; the **Rajska Dolina** ("Paradise Valley") chair works the sheltered eastern gully, the tree-protected option on a windy day; and the **Olimpijska** lift feeds the **Olympic run**, the 1984 women's course. Poljice, Rajska Dolina and Skočine are the three ticket-and-parking bases and interconnect on snow, roughly 52 km over 20-odd runs without touching a road. **Bjelašnica is a separate mountain with no ski link to Jahorina**: lifts climb from **Babin Do at 1,266 m** to the 2,067 m ridge, the men's 1984 downhill and slalom still in use, connecting across the plateau toward the **Igman** nordic area at Veliko and Malo Polje. **Trnovo** and **Šator** are the newer lift development on that side. **Last lifts 16:00**; the gap between mountains is patched by road only, **ski bus supplement 10 BAM**, with daily Sarajevo services to both.
raw.Snow reliability: Jahorina spans **1,300-1,916 m**, Bjelašnica **1,266-2,067 m**. Both sit in a continental Dinaric snow climate that produces genuinely heavy falls, this is one of the snowiest parts of Europe by annual total, but at low altitude and on a mountain whose upper dome is largely treeless. Jahorina's Rajska Dolina and Skočine sides face broadly north and east and hold; the Poljice base is the first thing to go. Both resorts run substantial snowmaking on the main descents, with Jahorina claiming near-full coverage of its principal pistes, but **no resort publishes snowmaking as a percentage of pisted kilometres, treat any figure you are quoted as marketing**. **Season: roughly 5 December to mid-April**, with the honest window mid-January to mid-March. In a bad snow year Jahorina retreats to Rajska Dolina and the upper Skočine runs and closes the ski-home to Poljice, sending you down in the gondola; Bjelašnica, higher and colder, usually keeps its summit runs when Jahorina's lower half has gone.
raw.Off-piste and touring: The serious ground is on Bjelašnica. The classic is the **plateau tour from Babin Do toward Šehitluci and the Studeni Potok drainage**, and the longer traverse to **Umoljani** and the rim of the **Rakitnica canyon**. Jahorina's off-piste is short tree skiing between the Skočine and Rajska Dolina pistes. **Critically, Bosnia and Herzegovina publishes no EAWS-standard daily avalanche bulletin.** The **Federalni hidrometeorološki zavod BiH (FHMZBiH)** and the **Republički hidrometeorološki zavod RS** give weather and snow-depth data, not a five-point hazard rating, read the snowpack yourself or hire someone who can. There is also **residual landmine risk around both massifs**: stay on marked ground and treat BHMAC hazard mapping as non-negotiable. **Guides: Green Visions**, the Sarajevo ecotourism operator, is the established outfit for Bjelašnica plateau snowshoe and touring days and for Lukomir; **Gorska služba spašavanja (GSS)** is mountain rescue.
raw.Piste breakdown: **Jahorina: roughly 52 km over 20 runs, about 25 km easy (48%), 24 km intermediate (46%), 3 km difficult (6%)**, plus 18 lifts. **Bjelašnica and Igman together add roughly 20 km** of steeper, more exposed terrain including the Olympic men's downhill. **Beginners** belong on the Poljice plateau and the wide lower half of the Skočine runs, where the pitch is gentle and the pistes are absurdly wide by Alpine standards. **Intermediates** own Jahorina outright: the Skočine reds and the full-width cruising off the Ogorjelica ridge are what this mountain does best. **Experts** get two things and should not expect a third, the **1984 Olympic run at Jahorina**, still a proper pitch, and the men's downhill line on Bjelašnica, which on a firm morning is the most serious piste in the country.
raw.Non-ski days: The **Trebević cable car** climbs from Bistrik in about nine minutes to 1,164 m; fifteen minutes' walk from the top station is the **abandoned 1984 bobsleigh and luge track**, a graffitied concrete serpent used as a wartime firing position, free, unfenced, affecting. In the city: the **Tunel spasa (Tunnel of Hope) Museum** at Butmir, the **Gazi Husrev-beg mosque and bezistan**, the **Historical Museum of BiH** siege exhibition, the **Svrzo House**. On the mountain: the **guided snowshoe traverse to Lukomir** (~1,495 m, the country's highest inhabited village) from Umoljani, and Jahorina's **tubing and Alpine Coaster** at Poljice. For warm water, **Terme Ilidža** west of the city and the restored **Isa-Begov Hamam** in the old town.
raw.Hire, lockers and schools: This is the cheapest instruction in ski Europe. Rental at the Poljice and Rajska Dolina bases and from the shops along the Jahorina hotel road runs roughly **25-40 BAM/day (€13, €20)** for a standard ski-boot-pole package, **120-200 BAM (€61, €102) for six days**; performance skis add 40-60%. Lockers at the base stations are 5-10 BAM/day. The **OC Jahorina ski school** and the independent schools attached to the larger hotels charge in the region of **40-70 BAM (€20, €36) per hour for a private lesson** and **150-260 BAM (€77, €133) for a five-morning group course**, roughly a third of Austrian rates. Book English-language instruction ahead; it exists but is not the default.

sources.confidenceNotes: **The 350 BAM combined Ski Card price dates from the scheme's introduction and must be re-verified for the current season.** **Bjelašnica's 6-day and multi-day rates were not found in any published tariff and are deliberately not quoted.** **Snowmaking coverage as a percentage of pisted km is not published by either resort**, no figure is invented here. Bjelašnica's altitude range (1,266-2,067 m) and the km attributed to Bjelašnica plus Igman are indicative. Named lifts (Poljice gondola, Skočine, Rajska Dolina, Olimpijska) are correct as sector/lift names, but type and capacity should be confirmed against the current trail map. Rental, ski-school, snowshoe-guide, locker and museum prices are indicative bands, not quoted tariffs. Season dates vary year to year. Hotel and restaurant names are real and long-established; check in-season opening. The landmine advisory is genuine, retain it.
